resolved_issues.title: [hmac] `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_PROCESS` commands causing hang conditions

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC) IP can hang while finalizing a SHA-256 hash when software writes the last message word into the HMAC message FIFO, waits briefly, and only then issues `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT`, the command that tells the hardware that no more message data is coming. The affected functionality is the SHA-2 finalization path inside the HMAC IP.

## Expected Behavior
After the last message word has been accepted, issuing `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` after a short delay must still finalize the pending message block, report that the hash operation is complete, and return the HMAC IP to idle. In software-visible terms, the idle bit in `HMAC.STATUS` (`hmac_idle`) must become set again instead of remaining cleared. This must also hold when the message length is exactly one full 512-bit SHA-256 block.

## Actual Behavior
With a short delay between the final FIFO write and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT`, the hash operation can remain stuck in a non-idle state. Completion is never reported, `HMAC.STATUS.hmac_idle` stays cleared, and software waiting for the HMAC hardware to become idle can block indefinitely.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when a block-aligned SHA-256 message is written to the HMAC message FIFO, the final 32-bit word completes the last 512-bit block, no further message words are written, and `HMAC_CMD_HASH_STOP_BIT` is issued only after a small delay such as interrupt latency.

title: [hmac,rtl] HMAC FSM fixes for SAR
body:
This implements RTL changes to the HMAC FSM to handle context switching (transitions to `StDone` to wait on hash result, and then `StIdle` from where every context ought to start/continue) and aligns triggering of idle and done. With this change, the SAR smoke test passes on @martin-velay's SAR DV branch (https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/23116) which tests out SAR across 2 contexts (HMAC + same digest size 256). 

This hasn't been tested out thoroughly, and I think other issues will come up as DV proceeds. I'm also running a block-level regression at my end. @ballifatih this should close this issue https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/23352, but I wouldn't be surprised if something else comes up next.

resolved_issues.title: [hmac, rtl] Reset hmac_core FSM to Idle after stop
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

I am trying to interleave two HMAC streams. Namely:

- Stream A (HMAC-384) starts and feeds some of its messages.
- Stream A is stopped and the state is saved to SW context.
- Stream B (HMAC-256) starts and feeds some of its messages.
- After around ~1000 bytes or so, Stream B hangs forever, and the initial symptom is MSG_FIFO being full. The test eventually fails with a timeout.

I tried to track down the signals which fetch entries from MSG_FIFO, and I eventually stumbled upon the main FSM of `hmac_core`. When I issue `start` for Stream B, I was expecting `sha_hash_start_o` (of `hmac_core`) signal to be raised, which does not happen.

I am looking at waveforms from a high-level, so I am not sure if it helps much, but here is the clock cycle when `start` command is sent over TL-UL (note the vertical marker). `st_q` of `hmac_core` is at `StMsg` even though HMAC  should have a clear state.
![image](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/assets/7850700/79d486f6-fd10-42d8-b6b7-624e96957d39)

Maybe we need a condition to go to `Idle` state from `StMsg` state, when `stop` is issued to HMAC HWIP. I do not understand the full interactions here to make a confident suggestion though.  


https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/0e5093d7098daf6b9b848e5c1ca6242336e731d3/hw/ip/hmac/rtl/hmac_core.sv#L352-L370

cc: @martin-velay @gdessouky @andreaskurth

problem_statement:
## Description
During save-and-restore or context-switching use of the OpenTitan HMAC IP, software may stop one HMAC stream, save its state, and then start a different stream. In the reported flow, Stream A is stopped, Stream B is started, and after roughly 1000 bytes Stream B stops making forward progress: the message input FIFO (`MSG_FIFO`) fills and the operation eventually times out. In this failure mode, the HMAC core still behaves as if the previous context is active when the second `start` command arrives.

## Affected Function
The bug is in the HMAC IP's `hmac_core` main state machine, specifically the logic that handles a `stop` request, returns the core to an idle state, and accepts a later `start` during save-and-restore or context-switch flows.

## Expected Behavior
After software issues `stop` for an active HMAC context, the core should finish the current message block, become idle once that block's hash operation completes, and then accept a later `start` for a different context. In that situation, the new `start` must raise the internal `sha_hash_start_o` start pulse and processing of the new stream must begin so that `MSG_FIFO` continues to drain.

## Actual Behavior
If `stop` is issued near the end of a later message block while the first context is still in the inner HMAC message-processing phase, the core may fail to return to its idle state after the current block completes. A subsequent `start` for another context then does not raise `sha_hash_start_o`, so the new stream never actually begins and its `MSG_FIFO` stops draining.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in HMAC save-and-restore or context-switching flows that stop one stream and start another while the first stream is still processing the inner part of a non-first SHA-2 message block. Reported examples include interleaving HMAC-384 and HMAC-256 streams, and the failure is reproducible in a long SHA-256/HMAC message when `stop` is asserted close to the end of a later block.

commits.message:
[csrng/rtl] Move cmd checks to the cmd stage

Having the command checks in the main SM doesn't make a lot of sense.
This causes a lot of issues including a hang condition inside the cmd stage
in case of generate commands with cmd len greater than 1. For this reason
it is best to not even start processing commands that violate our checks.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's CSRNG (Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator) accepts application commands through per-interface command staging logic (`cmd_stage`). The affected functionality is the CSRNG software application interface (`SW_APP`) command path in this staging logic. An unsupported application-command opcode can be accepted far enough into that path to leave the interface stuck instead of being rejected cleanly.

## Expected Behavior
If `SW_APP` submits an unsupported application command, CSRNG should treat it as a recoverable error without leaving that interface unusable. After the recoverable alert for the invalid request is handled and cleared, a later valid `instantiate` command followed by a valid `uninstantiate` command on the same interface should still complete normally and report successful completion.

## Actual Behavior
An unsupported command can raise the recoverable alert but still leave the `SW_APP` command staging path wedged. After that happens, later legal commands on the same interface may no longer complete as expected. In particular, a normal `instantiate` followed by `uninstantiate` sequence can stop reaching its completion indication even though both commands are valid.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered when the software application interface receives an unsupported generate-like application command that also carries extra command words, i.e. a nonzero command-length field (`clen`). The failure is especially visible with a multiword invalid request such as the reserved `GENU` opcode with `clen = 2`.

title: [i2c,rtl] Halt controller FSM when unexp. NAK is seen
body:
If the I2C bus NAKs any of our transfers when operating as a Controller-Transmitter in Byte-Formatted Programming Mode, the current behaviour is to proceed to the next FDATA entry as normal, disregarding the NAK entirely. The only side-effect of this event is the block raising the 'nak' interrupt (though this can be suppressed by the use of NAKOK in the FDATA entry).

This PR changes the behaviour so the Controller-FSM halts upon generation of the 'nak' interrupt, and proceeds once the interrupt has been acknowledged using the standard 'Event-Type' interrupt acknowledgement (W1C to INTR_STATE).
The next item in the FMTFIFO is not popped until this acknowledgement is received.
If the NAKOK bit is set for a particular Format Indicator and the bus NAKs our byte, the 'nak' interrupt is not asserted and the FSM continues to the next indicator in the fifo.

While the FSM is halted, SCL is released (we halt in the 'ClockPulseAck' state), and the bus is observed as having an elongated 9th clock period.

Two additional features are also added alongside this change.

- "HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT" CSR
This CSR controls a timeout mechanism where if SW does not handle a pending 'nak'
interrupt before the configured timeout elapses, the hardware will automatically
end the active transaction with a STOP condition and disable Host-Mode.

- "STATUS.HOST_DISABLED_NACK_TIMEOUT" bit
This bit is set when the block times out with the "HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT"
mechanism, and clears when SW re-enables Host-Mode. This is intended to inform
software that the timeout occurred.

The I2C agent / infrastructure does not currently support the generation of NAK's when operating as a Target-Receiver, so this PR also adds rudimentary support for this with a new Agent sequence, plus a test to exercise it (`i2c_host_may_nack`). The testbench currently models the SW interrupt handler latency with a fixed 1000-cycle delay. This should be expanded in the future.

TODO

- [x] Update documentation
- [ ] Check & Update TLTs

---

This new behaviour will need more comprehensive testing to achieve V2 quality. Our infrastructure to test this is currently incomplete, and will need to be expanded. I have observed some of the expected behaviour in an ad-hoc simulation, but it should not be considered fully robust until further testing is completed.

---

Closes #18917

resolved_issues.title: [i2c] Change FSM to stop processing the FMT_FIFO after receiving a NAK
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

From #18764:
Despite the IP registering a NAK, the transaction continues normally, when it should really stop and wait for software to clear the NAK condition. It turns out that there is nothing in the i2c FSM to prevent continuing with the next entry in the FIFO.

Fix this and document the expected handling from software.

@@ -0,0 +1,43 @@
+// Copyright lowRISC contributors.
+// Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0, see LICENSE for details.
+// SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+
+// I2C Agent sequence which behaves as an I2C TARGET.
+//
+// - Receives seq_items from req_analysis_fifo which are sent onto the driver.
+// - If the item is requesting to drive an ACK, 50/50 to change this to a NACK instead.
+//
+class i2c_target_may_nack_seq extends i2c_base_seq;
+  `uvm_object_utils(i2c_target_may_nack_seq)
+  `uvm_object_new
+
+  virtual task body();
+    case (cfg.if_mode)
+      Device: send_device_mode_txn();
+      Host:    `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "This sequence is for the agent in TARGET-Mode only!")
+      default: `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "Invalid cfg.if_mode!")
+    endcase
+  endtask : body
+
+  virtual task send_device_mode_txn();
+    bit [7:0] rdata;
+    forever begin
+      p_sequencer.req_analysis_fifo.get(req);
+      // If it's a read type response, create randomized return data
+      if (req.drv_type == RdData) begin
+        `DV_CHECK_STD_RANDOMIZE_FATAL(rdata)
+        req.rdata = rdata;
+      end
+      // Convert some of the 'DevAck' items from the monitor into NACKs
+      if (req.drv_type == DevAck) begin
+        if ($urandom_range(0, 1)) begin
+          `uvm_info(`gfn, "Converting an ACK to a NACK!", UVM_LOW)
+          req.drv_type = DevNack;
+        end
+      end
+      start_item(req);
+      finish_item(req);
+    end
+  endtask
+
+endclass : i2c_target_may_nack_seq
diff --git a/hw/ip/i2c/data/i2c.hjson b/hw/ip/i2c/data/i2c.hjson

+++ b/hw/ip/i2c/data/i2c.hjson
@@ -204,7 +204,8 @@
     { name: "CTRL"
       desc: "I2C Control Register"
       swaccess: "rw"
-      hwaccess: "hro"
+      hwaccess: "hrw"
+      hwqe:     "true",
       fields: [
         { bits: "0"
           resval: "0"
@@ -284,6 +285,13 @@
           desc: "Target mode receive FIFO is empty"
           resval: "1"
         }
+        { bits: "10"
+          name: "HOST_DISABLED_NACK_TIMEOUT"
+          desc: '''
+                A Host-Mode active transaction has been ended by the !!HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT mechanism.
+                This bit is cleared when !!CTRL.ENABLEHOST is set by software to start a new transaction.
+                '''
+        }
       ]
       tags: [// Updated by the hw. Exclude from write-checks.
              "excl:CsrNonInitTests:CsrExclWriteCheck"]
@@ -683,7 +691,14 @@
       ]
     }
     { name: "HOST_TIMEOUT_CTRL"
-      desc: "I2C host clock generation timeout value (in units of input clock frequency)"
+      desc: '''
+            I2C host clock generation timeout value (in units of input clock frequency).
+
+            In an active transaction in Target-Mode, if the Controller ceases to send SCL pulses
+            for this number of cycles then the "host_timeout" interrupt will be asserted.
+
+            Set this CSR to 0 to disable this behaviour.
+            '''
       swaccess: "rw"
       hwaccess: "hro"
       fields: [
@@ -721,5 +736,37 @@
         { bits: "7:0" }
       ]
     }
+    { name: "HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT"
+      desc: '''
+            Timeout in Host-Mode for an unhandled NACK before hardware automatically ends the transaction.
+            (in units of input clock frequency)
+
+            In Host-Mode during an active Controller-Transmitter transfer, if the Target NACKs a byte
+            the 'nak' interrupt is asserted and the Byte-Formatted Programming Mode FSM halts awaiting
+            software intervention. Software must acknowledge the interrupt (CIP 'Event-Type') to allow
+            the state machine to continue, typically after clearing out the FMTFIFO to start a new transfer.
+            While halted, the active transaction is not ended (no STOP (P) condition is created), and the
+            block releases both SCL and SDA.
+
+            This timeout can be used to automatically disable the block if software does not handle the
+            'nak' interrupt in a timely manner. If the timeout expires, (!!CTRL.HOSTMODE) will be disabled
+            which creates a STOP (P) condition on the bus ending the active transaction. Additionally, the
+            !!STATUS.HOST_DISABLED_NACK_TIMEOUT bit is set to alert software.
+
+            The enable bit must be set for this feature to operate.
+            '''
+      swaccess: "rw"
+      hwaccess: "hro"
+      fields: [
+        { bits: "30:0"
+          name: "VAL"
+          desc: "Unhandled NAK timeout value (in units of input clock frequency)"
+        }
+        { bits: "31"
+          name: "EN"
+          desc: "Timeout enable"
+        }
+      ]
+    }
   ]
 }

+## HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT
+Timeout in Host-Mode for an unhandled NACK before hardware automatically ends the transaction.
+(in units of input clock frequency)
+
+In Host-Mode during an active Controller-Transmitter transfer, if the Target NACKs a byte
+the 'nak' interrupt is asserted and the Byte-Formatted Programming Mode FSM halts awaiting
+software intervention. Software must acknowledge the interrupt (CIP 'Event-Type') to allow
+the state machine to continue, typically after clearing out the FMTFIFO to start a new transfer.
+While halted, the active transaction is not ended (no STOP (P) condition is created), and the
+block releases both SCL and SDA.
+
+This timeout can be used to automatically disable the block if software does not handle the
+'nak' interrupt in a timely manner. If the timeout expires, ([`CTRL.HOSTMODE`](#ctrl)) will be disabled
+which creates a STOP (P) condition on the bus ending the active transaction. Additionally, the
+[`STATUS.HOST_DISABLED_NACK_TIMEOUT`](#status) bit is set to alert software.
+
+The enable bit must be set for this feature to operate.

+#### Halt-on-NAK
+
+If the Host-Mode Controller-Transmitter transmits a byte and the 9th bit is a NACK from the Target/Bus, the `nak` interrupt is usually asserted (modulo the effect of [`FDATA.NAKOK`](registers.md#fdata)).
+If the 'nak' interrupt is asserted, the Byte-Formatted Programming Mode FSM will halt until the interrupt has been acknowledged using the standard 'Event-Type' interrupt acknowledgement (W1C to INTR_STATE).
+Software will likely want to do one of two things in handling this irq:
+1. End the current transaction by setting [`CTRL.ENABLEHOST`](registers.md#ctrl) to `1'b0`, and clear the FIFOs ready to begin a new transaction.
+2. Clear the FIFOs, then begin a new transfer without ending the transaction by add new FDATA indicators to the FMTFIFO.
+   In this case, the first entry written to the FMTFIFO should have [`FDATA.START`](registers.md#fdata) set to `1'b1` to create a repeated start condition.
+
+While the FSM is halted, SCL/SDA are released and the bus is observed as having an elongated 9th clock period.
+
+The Halt-on-'NAK' behaviour may be problematic if SW is not responsive, so there is a timeout mechanism that can automatically end the transaction by creating a STOP condition and disabling Host-Mode.
+This is configured using the [`HOST_NACK_HANDLER_TIMEOUT`](registers.md#host_nack_handler_timeout) CSR, which allows software to configure the delay before hardware will terminate the transaction.
+Hardware will also automatically clear [`CTRL.ENABLEHOST`](registers.md#ctrl) when this occurs.
+If this mechanism activates, software can be informed by reading the [`STATUS.HOST_DISABLED_NACK_TIMEOUT`](registers.md#status) bit.
+This field is cleared when software next activates Host-Mode by setting [`CTRL.ENABLEHOST`](registers.md#ctrl) to `1'b1`.
+Before re-activating Host-Mode, software should ensure that the 'nak' interrupt has been handled and acknowledged.
+

+  `uvm_object_utils(i2c_host_may_nack_vseq)
+  `uvm_object_new
+
+  virtual task i2c_init(if_mode_e mode = Host);
+    super.i2c_init();
+    // Mask some interrupts that are just noise for this test.
+    ral.intr_enable.fmt_threshold.set(1'b0);
+    ral.intr_enable.tx_threshold.set(1'b0);
+    ral.intr_enable.sda_interference.set(1'b0);
+    ral.intr_enable.scl_interference.set(1'b0);

+    ral.intr_enable.stretch_timeout.set(1'b0);

+
+    // Enable the 'nak' timeout feature, but with a longer timeout than our handler latency.
+    ral.host_nack_handler_timeout.en.set(1'b1);
+    ral.host_nack_handler_timeout.val.set(30'd5000);
+    csr_update(ral.host_nack_handler_timeout);
+  endtask
+
+  // Override the base vseq method to configure an agent which may sometime NACK
+  virtual task agent_init(if_mode_e mode = Device);

+
+    case (mode)
+      Device: begin
+        `uvm_create_obj(i2c_target_may_nack_seq, may_nack_seq)

+      end
+      Host:    `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "This vseq requires the agent to be in TARGET-Mode!")
+      default: `uvm_fatal(`gfn, "Invalid 'if_mode'!")
+    endcase
+  endtask : agent_init
+
+endclass : i2c_host_may_nack_vseq

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan I2C IP mishandles an unexpected negative acknowledgment (NACK) in host mode when it is acting as a controller-transmitter in Byte-Formatted Programming Mode, where software queues host format commands in the format FIFO through FDATA entries. If the target acknowledges the address byte but then NACKs a transmitted data byte, the controller records the NACK but can still advance to the next queued format entry instead of pausing at the failed byte.

## Expected Behavior
After an unexpected NACK in this host-mode transmit path, the I2C controller must stop consuming additional FDATA / format FIFO entries and keep the active transaction paused until software clears the pending `nak` interrupt. While the NACK is pending, the controller must remain in an active host transaction rather than returning to host-idle state, and queued format entries must remain in the FIFO instead of being drained.

## Actual Behavior
The current implementation raises the `nak` interrupt but continues processing the queued transfer. In the reproduced case where the address phase is ACKed and the first queued data byte is NACKed, later queued bytes can still be consumed and the transfer can continue before software clears the interrupt.

## Affected Function
This affects the OpenTitan I2C IP's host-mode byte-formatting controller finite state machine (FSM), specifically the logic that handles ACK/NACK results after transmitting a byte and decides whether to pop the next format FIFO entry.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when the I2C block is operating in host mode as a controller-transmitter, software has queued multiple FDATA entries for a write transaction, the target acknowledges the address byte, and the target then NACKs the first queued data byte before software has cleared the pending NACK condition.

title: [rtl,pwrmgr] Fix escalation timeout persistence
body:
The escalation timeout needs to persist until reset. The timeout is detected by clk_i, but the timeout is used to drive a flop clocked by clk_lc. This change adds a synchronizer from clk_i to clk_lc, and a clk_lc flop reset by rst_lc_n. The output of this flop is used to set the fault_status and as a reset request.

Fixes #20516

commits.message:
[rtl,pwrmgr] Fix escalation timeout persistence

The escalation timeout needs to persist until reset. The timeout is detected by
clk_i, but the timeout is used to drive a flop clocked by clk_lc. This change
adds a synchronizer from clk_i to clk_lc, and a clk_lc flop reset by rst_lc_n.
The output of this flop is used to set the fault_status and as a reset request.

With this fix the pwrmgr_escalation_reset test passes at the block level.

Fixes #20516

Signed-off-by: Guillermo Maturana <maturana@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [rtl,pwrmgr] escalation timeout should persist
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

If the escalation network stops for more than 128 cycles, pwrmgr should request an escalation reset, per https://opentitan.org/book/hw/top_earlgrey/ip_autogen/pwrmgr/doc/theory_of_operation.html#escalation-clock-timeout.

However, the escalation timeout condition (esc_timeout in pwrmgr.sv) does not persist, unlike esc_rst_req_d/q. This means if the escalation clock restarts soon after 128 cycles of being inactive an escalation reset won't be generated.

One simple fix would be to flop esc_timeout, similar to how esc_rst_req_d is treated.

tb_script:
#!/bin/bash
set -u -o pipefail

cd /home/opentitan || exit 1
export PATH="/tools/riscv/bin:/tools/verible/bin:$PATH"

TEST_NAME="pwrmgr_escalation_timeout_persist"
TB_ROOT="/home/opentitan/.tb_pwrmgr_escalation_timeout"
SCRATCH_ROOT="${TB_ROOT}/scratch"
LOG_PATH="${TB_ROOT}/dvsim.log"

emit_result() {
  local status="$1"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"
  echo "TEST: ${TEST_NAME} ... ${status}"
  echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"
}

mkdir -p "${TB_ROOT}"
rm -rf "${SCRATCH_ROOT}"

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path

paths = [
    Path("hw/top_earlgrey/ip_autogen/pwrmgr/dv/env/seq_lib/pwrmgr_escalation_timeout_vseq.sv"),
    Path("hw/ip_templates/pwrmgr/dv/env/seq_lib/pwrmgr_escalation_timeout_vseq.sv"),
]
old = "    // check_stopped_esc_clk(136, 1'b1);\n"
new = "    check_stopped_esc_clk(136, 1'b1);\n"

for path in paths:
    text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    if new in text:
        continue
    if old not in text:
        raise SystemExit(f"marker not found in {path}")
    path.write_text(text.replace(old, new, 1), encoding="utf-8")
PY
prep_rc=$?
if [[ ${prep_rc} -ne 0 ]]; then
  emit_result "FAIL"
  exit "${prep_rc}"
fi

set +e
timeout 1800 ./util/dvsim/dvsim.py \
  hw/top_earlgrey/ip_autogen/pwrmgr/dv/pwrmgr_sim_cfg.hjson \
  -i pwrmgr_escalation_timeout \
  -t vcs \
  --local \
  --fixed-seed 2 \
  --build-seed 1 \
  --scratch-root "${SCRATCH_ROOT}" \
  --purge \
  --max-parallel 1 \
  --build-timeout-mins 20 \
  --run-timeout-mins 10 \
  --no-rerun \
  -v m \
  2>&1 | tee "${LOG_PATH}"
rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
set -e

if [[ ${rc} -eq 0 ]]; then
  emit_result "PASS"
else
  emit_result "FAIL"
fi
exit "${rc}"

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's Power Manager (pwrmgr) contains escalation clock-timeout logic that is supposed to detect when the alert escalation path stops responding while the system is in its normal active state. If the escalation clock remains inactive for more than 128 pwrmgr clock cycles, pwrmgr must treat that as an escalation fault and initiate a local escalation reset.

## Expected Behavior
A stall shorter than the 128-cycle timeout threshold must not trigger an escalation reset. Once the escalation clock has been inactive long enough to exceed that threshold, the timeout condition must persist until reset handling takes effect. Even if the escalation clock starts toggling again shortly after the threshold is crossed, pwrmgr must still disable CPU fetch and issue the escalation reset request.

## Actual Behavior
The timeout condition is not persistent. If the escalation clock stops for only slightly more than the timeout threshold and then restarts soon afterward, pwrmgr can lose the fault indication before the reset path reacts to it. In that case, CPU fetch remains enabled and no escalation reset request is generated even though the timeout threshold was exceeded.

## Trigger Condition
This bug is triggered in the pwrmgr escalation timeout path when the escalation clock is halted just over the 128-cycle limit and then restarted before the fault has been latched as a persistent reset condition. Very long stalls still trigger the reset reliably, so the failure is most visible in near-threshold cases.

title: [mbx] Improve Abort handling, and recovery from communications failure.
body:
This PR implements a FW-initiated reset of the Inbound and Outbound data paths in the event of a communications failure within the SoC<->mailbox<->TL-UL chain and improves the Abort handling.

_Mailbox operation is critical to all communication between the SoC and RoT, and use of the asynchronous reset of the IP block is considered infeasible because it is common to many other IP blocks._


The logic is currently reliant upon everything completing as expected (whether successfully or by an error being indicated by the TL-UL device/bus), but is not robust against potential design flaws nor against any reliability issues with the specific physical device. Further, the current Error and Abort handling mechanisms do not have the capacity to reset fully the internal state of the mailbox logic. ([Issue detailed here](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan-integrated/issues/708).)

To help with understanding this PR, the Abort mechanism is described below:

- in the event of a failure in the Request/Response mechanism, the SoC side has the capacity to request that an operation be Aborted and it is expected that this mechanism be used in response to a communications timeout (of the order of > 1 second).
- the Abort request is signaled to the RoT via an interrupt.
- the RoT firmware acknowledges the Abort condition.

It is worth noting that the SoC side itself may become stalled and unable to employ the Abort mechanism, since a Write Data access from the SoC when sending the Request may cause the SoC to be blocked upon completion of the previous write. Similarly, a Read Data access from the SoC when fetching the Response will block until the read data is retrieved from the mailbox SRAM.

It is therefore proposed that the Abort acknowledgment should be available as a RoT FW-initiated reset of the mailbox logic, for use even if there has been no explicit Abort request from the SoC side.

This PR consists of two commits:

**Commit 1:** Introduces a reset of the following internal state when the RoT FW ('host') acknowledges an Abort condition.

- u_ombx.u_req_state <- TL-UL read request
- u_ombx.u_pop_entry <- ditto
- u_ombx.u_pending <- SoC side Write Data Register stall
- u_imbx.u_req_state <- TL-UL write request
- u_imbx.u_pending <- ditto

It also clears down the count of outstanding TL-UL bus requests (`u_sramrwarb.u_outstanding_req_cnt`) and suppresses any subsequent TL-UL read response from being propagated into the Outbound mailbox logic, because that previously would result in the logic re-entering an active state as if starting to send a fresh Response to the SoC side.

**Commit 2:** Prioritizes the host-side Abort acknowledgement over all FSM states such that it may be used as a FW-initiated reset at any time, and not just when handling an explicit Abort request from the SoC. This would be used after a timeout in the communications from/to the SoC side. (Apologies: This changes the FSM identation and confuses diff tools.)

This should address [issue 708](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan-integrated/issues/708) although DV is currently unable to verify the existing Abort handling or the complete efficacy of this change. The smoke test still passes as expected.

commits.message:
[mbx] Fault recovery via Abort mechanism

Clearing of Abort condition resets both inbound and outbound
traffic, clears down the count of outstanding requests and
suppresses any subsequent core-side TL-UL read responses.
Since the Abort request clears Ready, keep the Read Data
register zeroed until the abort is acknowledged.

Signed-off-by: Adrian Lees <a.lees@lowrisc.org>

[mbx] Abort acknowledgement always resets FSMs.

Abort acknowledgement is of the highest priority, permitting
its use as a FW-driven reset mechanism even if there was no
explicit SoC-side Abort request.

Signed-off-by: Adrian Lees <a.lees@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [hmac] Revise localparams to have unique and meaningful names
resolved_issues.body:
The issue #701 is reported by @imphil

Problem:

    Previous version of `hmac_pkg.sv` has duplicated names `k`. `k` is
    used as localparam and also used as an argument in `compress()`
    function.

The `k` in localparam is the first 32bit of fractional part for the
cubic root of the first 64 primes. So the name is changed to have the
meaning.

problem_statement:
## Description
OpenTitan's mailbox (mbx) IP carries request and response traffic between the SoC and the Root of Trust (RoT). The inbound mailbox accepts request data written by the SoC, and the outbound mailbox presents response data for the SoC to read. After a communication failure or timeout on this path, RoT firmware must be able to acknowledge the abort condition and use that acknowledgement as a firmware-driven reset of the mailbox control logic, even when the SoC cannot complete the normal abort handshake first.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the mbx IP's inbound and outbound mailbox control state machines, including the outbound Ready indication during abort recovery.

## Expected Behavior
When RoT firmware acknowledges the abort condition, the mailbox must immediately return to its idle state regardless of which mailbox FSM state is currently active. This must work while the inbound mailbox is already in its write phase and while the outbound mailbox is already in its read/response phase. For an outbound transaction, the same abort acknowledgement must also clear the Ready indication for the aborted response. After that reset, the mailbox must be able to start a new inbound or outbound transaction normally.

## Actual Behavior
In the current implementation, an abort acknowledgement from RoT firmware is not honored once the mailbox FSM has already left idle. If the inbound mailbox is already accepting write data, or the outbound mailbox is already in its read/response phase, the FSM can remain in its active state instead of returning to idle. On the outbound side, Ready can also remain asserted for an aborted response. As a result, the aborted transaction is not fully cleared and the mailbox does not reliably recover for the next transaction.

## Trigger Condition
This bug is triggered when a mailbox transaction is already active and RoT firmware acknowledges the abort condition during recovery from a communication failure or timeout. It also occurs when that acknowledgement is used as a firmware-driven reset without a preceding SoC-side abort request, which is needed when the SoC is stalled and cannot complete the explicit abort sequence.

title: [edn] Clear auto cmd FIFOs after edn disable
body:
This PR clears the auto cmd FIFOs after the edn is disabled.
For more precise information check out the individual commit messages.

This PR resolves #19653

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
[edn] Reset auto cmd FIFOs when EDN is disabled

This commit resets the auto mode cmd FIFOs whenever the EDN is disabled.
This is done by setting the main_sm_done_pulse_o to high whenever the
edn_enable_i signal changes to low. In edn_core.sv, the done_pulse is used
for several purposes other than just resetting the FIFOs. However, this change
has no or little impact for the other three use cases of this signal. In two of
those three cases the done_pulse has no impact, since the EDN is disabled and the
multiplexer ignores the pulse. In the third case the max_num_between_reseeds is
loaded into a counter whenever the done_pulse is high. This should be fine since the
CSRNG is initialized anyways, should the EDN enter auto mode at a later time.
The only difference for the third case would be that when the auto mode is left
through disabling the EDN, the counter is now reset and should it re-enter auto
mode the counter starts counting from 0 again. This didn't use to be the case.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

[edn] Get the DV environment in line with resetting FIFOs after EDN is disabled

This commit gets the DV environment in line with the prior change. This includes
waiting for the EDN to be enabled before disabling in edn_disable_auto_req_mode_vseq.
It also includes an update for the tracing of the scoreboard FIFOs.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

[edn/doc] Update documentation to explain when auto cmd FIFOs are cleared

This commit updates the documentation to make it more clear when exactly
the auto command FIFOs are cleared.

Signed-off-by: Hakim Filali <hfilali@lowrisc.org>

resolved_issues.title: [edn] Discussion on Generate/Reseed cmd FIFOs behavior when disabling EDN
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

Currently the Reseed_cmd and the Generate_cmd FIFOs get cleared whenever the CTRL. CMD_FIFO_RST flag is set to true or when the edn_main_sm generates a done pulse. A done_pulse is generated on 3 different occasions:

1. Then edn_main_sm transitions from the BootPulse to the BootDone state (in boot_req_mode)
2. The edn_main_sm transitions from the AutoDispatch to the Idle state (when auto_req_mode is disabled)
3. The edn_main_sm transitions from the Idle state to the sw_port_mode state (when boot/auto_req_mode are both disabled)

The FIFOs aren't cleared however, when the EDN is disabled. E.g. the transition from the AutoDispatch to the Idle state could also happen when the EDN is disabled. In that case, the FIFOs aren't cleared. Even though it has the same initial and final state as point 2.

We should discuss if this is the intended behavior. And if not, when do we want to clear the FIFOs?

The results of this discussion should be added to the documentation.

FYI: @vogelpi @andreaskurth

problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in the Entropy Distribution Network (EDN) auto request shutdown path. In auto request mode, EDN stores the programmed `GENERATE_CMD` and `RESEED_CMD` sequences in replay FIFOs so it can resend them to the Cryptographically Secure Random Number Generator (CSRNG). When firmware disables EDN by clearing `CTRL.EDN_ENABLE` while auto request mode is still configured, the EDN main state machine can return to `Idle` without clearing those replay FIFOs.

## Expected Behavior
Disabling EDN must fully terminate the current auto request session. Once the disable transition completes and the EDN main state machine reaches `Idle`, both auto-command replay FIFOs for `GENERATE_CMD` and `RESEED_CMD` must be empty, just as they are after `CTRL.CMD_FIFO_RST`, after boot-time completion, or after leaving auto request mode by clearing `CTRL.AUTO_REQ_MODE`. No command words from the previous auto request session should remain queued after the block has been disabled.

## Actual Behavior
If EDN is disabled directly from an active auto request state, stale generate and reseed command words can remain queued even after the block returns to `Idle`. The disable path does not leave the EDN in a clean disabled state.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the EDN auto request control path, specifically the EDN main state machine and the replay FIFOs that hold automatic `generate` and `reseed` commands for CSRNG traffic.

## Trigger Condition
Program EDN for auto request mode, populate the `GENERATE_CMD` and `RESEED_CMD` replay FIFOs, and then disable EDN by clearing `CTRL.EDN_ENABLE` without first leaving auto request mode through `CTRL.AUTO_REQ_MODE`. The bug appears when the disable path forces the EDN main state machine back to `Idle` from an active auto request state.

resolved_issues.title: [edn] Don't propagate SW commands after a fatal error
resolved_issues.body:
bad029c9c7 fixes the propagation of SW commands, so that writes to the `SW_CMD_REQ` register don’t propagate in multiple Auto mode states. The default assignment in EDN’s main FSM still allows the propagation of SW commands, though, and these default assignments apply even to the fatal error state. **Thus, SW can send commands to CSRNG even if EDN is in the fatal error state.** A CSRNG command that returns `genbits` will get those bits stored in EDN’s internal FIFOs. EDN’s endpoints cannot access the entropy in the fatal error state, however, because the acknowledge FSM stops acknowledging requests. We don’t test this case currently, but we do have the `EdnFatalAlertNoRsp_A` assertion, which ensures that EDN does not acknowledge any requests in the fatal alert state.

**For D3, we should tweak the main FSM so that it only propagates SW commands when needed (and certainly not in the fatal alert state).**

resolved_issues.title: [edn] Should SW commands be allowed in boot_req_mode
resolved_issues.body:
### Description

In the documentation it says :

> In boot-time request mode, the command sequence is fully hardware-controlled and no command customization is possible. In this mode, the EDN automatically issues a special reduced-latency instantiate command followed by the default generate commands. This means, for instance, that no personalization strings or additional data may be passed to the CSRNG application interface port in this mode. On exiting, the EDN issues an uninstantiate command to destroy the associated CSRNG instance.

However, in the RTL I couldn't find anything that keeps SW commands from being issued in boot_req_mode. I also observed SW commands in the tests while CTRL.BOOT_REQ_MODE was set to true. 

Looking at the RTL code I think it is possible that sw commands can be issued in boot mode. It just relies on the SM not being in any of the following states: AutoSendGenCmd, AutoSendReseedCmd, AutoAckWait, AutoDispatch, AutoCaptGenCnt, AutoCaptReseedCnt, BootSendGenCmd or BootLoadIns. Other than in those states, a sw command can be issued if (reg2hw.sw_cmd_req.qe & sw_cmd_valid) is equal to 1’b1. [This](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/17083/commits/793f168b1e18a00c6f2ce63389668af64b7b0981) commit also aligns with the stated above.

If we decide to change the RTL, [this](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/17083/commits/793f168b1e18a00c6f2ce63389668af64b7b0981) commit could be extended to exclude more states. But in my opinion a cleaner solution could be to add a signal in the main_sm, that is high whenever the sm is in the AutoLoadIns or the SW_Port_Mode state. This way we could disallow sw commands unless the above signal is high.

If we decide to keep things as they are we may consider to adapt the documentation.

Another thing to consider is that the SM is in the BootDone state when the boot sequence is done. It stays there until the EDN is disabled or an error occurs. We could also discuss adding a transition from BootDone to Idle when the CTRL.BOOT_REQ_MODE flag is disabled. This might make the RTL align more with the quote from the documentation below, since atm disabling CTRL.BOOT_REQ_MODE doesn't cause the SM to leave the BootDone state. To my observation, there is also no uninstatiate command being issued when exiting boot mode.

> Once firmware initialization is complete, it is important to exit this mode if the endpoints ever need FIPS-approved random values. This is done by either clearing the EDN_ENABLE field or clearing the BOOT_REQ_MODE field in [CTRL](https://opentitan.org/book/hw/ip/edn/doc/registers.html#ctrl) to halt the boot-time request state machine. Firmware must then wait for successful the shutdown of the state machine by polling the REQ_MODE_SM_STS field of the [SUM_STS](https://opentitan.org/book/hw/ip/edn/doc/registers.html#sum_sts) register.

FYI: @vogelpi @andreaskurth

problem_statement:
## Description
The EDN (Entropy Distribution Network) IP does not cleanly hand control from boot-time request mode back to its normal software command path. After the boot-time sequence finishes, the EDN main state machine reaches `BootDone`; clearing `CTRL.BOOT_REQ_MODE` while keeping the EDN enabled is supposed to exit boot-time request mode and return the block to software-driven operation.

## Expected Behavior
When the boot-time sequence has completed and firmware clears `CTRL.BOOT_REQ_MODE` without disabling the EDN, the EDN main state machine should leave `BootDone`, enter the normal software-port state (`SWPortMode`), and report that the software command interface is ready again so firmware can submit normal post-boot commands through the EDN software port.

## Actual Behavior
After the boot-time sequence completes, clearing `CTRL.BOOT_REQ_MODE` can leave the EDN stuck in `BootDone` instead of transitioning into software-port operation. The software command path therefore does not report ready for normal post-boot commands.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the EDN main state machine path that handles the handoff from boot-time request mode to the normal software-port mode.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when the EDN is enabled in boot-time request mode, the configured boot-time sequence runs to completion, firmware clears `CTRL.BOOT_REQ_MODE` while keeping the EDN enabled, and firmware then attempts to use the EDN software command interface.

title: fix(spid): Latch FIFOADDR at correct time
body:
_Related Issue: https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/15266_

This PR fixes a bug for unaligned access in TPM read commands.

fifoaddr is latched with the counter being `'h1F`. The counter, however, runs on SPI_CLK, while the latching logic is running on inverted SPI_CLK domain.

As a result, the latching logic captures the fifo address at a cycle earlier with prematured address. So it always assume address[1] as address[0].

This commit fixes the issue by:

1. Convert `sck_fifoaddr_latch` into iSCK domain.
2. To not shift the address one bit more, use `sck_cmdaddr_wdata_q` rather than `sck_cmdaddr_wdata_d`.

resolved_issues.body:
@eunchan 

In this case, the address is 'hf05. Since TPM_RID is only 1 bytes, design should return 'hff.
Looks like the address latch point is half cycle earlier, so that it got 'hf04.
![Screen Shot 2022-10-04 at 1 41 46 PM](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/49293026/193923306-21b56d0f-c677-4aa8-b425-2d03aba28dd8.png)

Waves and saved session:
/mnt/disks/filestores/opentitan-shared/users/weicai/scratch/fix/spi_device-sim-vcs/0.spi_device_tpm_read_hw_reg/latest

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_tpm.sv b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_tpm.sv
index e7ed24dc68e81..3348242081390 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_tpm.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_tpm.sv
@@ -353,6 +353,8 @@ module spi_tpm
 
   logic [FifoRegSize-1:0] isck_fifoaddr; // latched from sck_cmdaddr_wdata_d
   logic                   sck_fifoaddr_latch;
+  // isck_fifoaddr_latch converts sck_fifoaddr_latch by half SPI_CLK period.
+  logic                   isck_fifoaddr_latch;
 
   logic isck_fifoaddr_inc;
 
@@ -523,8 +525,39 @@ module spi_tpm
 
   assign check_hw_reg = (cmdaddr_bitcnt == 5'h 1D);
 
+  // sck_fifoaddr_latch & isck_fifoaddr_latch.
+  //
+  // isck_fifoaddr_latch is used to latch `isck_fifoaddr` as the name implies.
+  // The sck_fifoaddr_latch is high at the last beat of the address field as
+  // shown below.
+  //           _   _   _   _   _
+  // SPI_CLK _/ \_/ \_/ \_/ \_/ \_
+  //           ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
+  // bitcnt   X 0 X ..X 1EX 1FX
+  //
+  // But the data is valid second half of the 'h 1F phase. However, the
+  // latching logic latches @ clk_out_i (Inverted SPI_CLK). So it latches at
+  // a cycle earlier.
+  //
+  //                       | err here
+  //            _   _   _   _   _
+  // iSPI_CLK _/ \_/ \_/ \_/ \_/ \_
+  //         ___ ___ ___ ___ ___
+  // bitcnt  X 0 X ..X 1EX 1FX
+  //
+  //
+  // isck_fifoaddr_latch delays sck_fifoaddr_latch for the logic latches the
+  // address correctly.
   assign sck_fifoaddr_latch = (cmdaddr_bitcnt == 5'h 1F);
 
+  always_ff @(posedge clk_out_i or negedge rst_n) begin
+    if (!rst_n) begin
+      isck_fifoaddr_latch <= 1'b 0;
+    end else begin
+      isck_fifoaddr_latch <= sck_fifoaddr_latch;
+    end
+  end
+
   always_ff @(posedge clk_in_i or negedge rst_n) begin
     if (!rst_n) begin
       sck_cmdaddr_wdata_q <= '0;
@@ -543,10 +576,9 @@ module spi_tpm
   always_ff @(posedge clk_out_i or negedge rst_n) begin
     if (!rst_n) begin
       isck_fifoaddr <= '0;
-    end else if (sck_fifoaddr_latch) begin
-      // TODO: latch sck_fifoaddr_latch into isck_fifoaddr_latch?
+    end else if (isck_fifoaddr_latch) begin
       // Shall assert when sck_st_q moves away from StAddr
-      isck_fifoaddr <= sck_cmdaddr_wdata_d[FifoRegSize-1:0];
+      isck_fifoaddr <= sck_cmdaddr_wdata_q[FifoRegSize-1:0];
     end else if (isck_fifoaddr_inc) begin
       isck_fifoaddr <= isck_fifoaddr + 1'b 1;
     end

problem_statement:
## Description
A bug exists in the SPI Device IP's Trusted Platform Module (TPM) read path for TPM hardware-returned registers. When the SPI Device is configured in TPM FIFO mode and the SPI host performs an unaligned TPM read, the device can use the previous byte address instead of the requested byte address.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the SPI Device IP's TPM hardware-register read handling in TPM FIFO mode, including reads of hardware-returned registers such as `TPM_RID`.

## Expected Behavior
The SPI Device must return data for the exact byte address requested by the SPI host. For the 1-byte `TPM_RID` register at offset `0xF04`, a 1-byte TPM read from address `0xD4_0F05` must return `0xFF`, because that byte is outside the implemented width of `TPM_RID`.

## Actual Behavior
A 1-byte TPM read from address `0xD4_0F05` can be interpreted as a read from `0xD4_0F04`, so the SPI Device returns the `TPM_RID` value instead of `0xFF`.

## Trigger Condition
This failure occurs when the SPI Device is operating in TPM FIFO mode, TPM hardware registers are returned directly by hardware, and the SPI host issues an unaligned TPM read to a hardware-returned register. The reported failing example is a 1-byte read of `TPM_RID` at address `0xD4_0F05`.

title: [i2c] fix how sda_interference is detected.
body:
- fixes #15067
- instead of checking the input value immediately after changing sda, we instead wait through the rise time and sychronization delays.
- After waiting through that delay, if the input does not match the output, then assert sda interference.

In the process of making this fix, the fsm was simplified a tiny bit on the host side.  The SetupBit states were removed since they do not serve any function.  There is no need for the host to wait until the setup window before driving its output.

Additioanlly, minor fixes were made to the testbench to correct some of the ack and nak sampling behavior.

Signed-off-by: Timothy Chen <timothytim@google.com>

resolved_issues.title: [i2c] incorrect sda_intereference detection
resolved_issues.body:
credit to @a-will for discovering this.

the i2c sda_interference detection is done in the same cycle.
Meaning, if the i2c fsm decides to drive sda high, it must observe the incoming `sda_i` is also high in the same cycle.
This is impossible, as `sda_i` is synchronized and can never be the same value on a transition. Even if there were no synchronization, it could still be difficult for `sda_i` to be the same value in the same cycle because `i2c` is inherently an interface with slow rise times. 

This bug was masked by #15066.

problem_statement:
## Description
The affected functionality is the OpenTitan I2C IP host-side finite state machine (FSM) that raises the `sda_interference` event/interrupt when the host controller believes SDA (Serial Data) is being held low by another device. In I2C, driving a logical 1 on SDA means releasing the open-drain line so an external pull-up can bring it high. Because the sampled SDA input (`sda_i`) passes through an input synchronizer and the bus has non-zero rise time, the sampled value is allowed to remain low for a short time after the host releases SDA.

## Expected Behavior
When the host releases SDA and expects it to be high, the controller must allow enough time for a legal SDA rise to propagate through the bus and input synchronizer before declaring interference. On an uncontended bus, a clean host transaction, including a host read transaction, must not raise `sda_interference` just because SDA is still low for a few cycles immediately after release; the transfer should continue and complete normally.

## Actual Behavior
The host-side FSM checks for SDA interference in the same cycle that it changes SDA from driven low to released high. As a result, the controller can compare its newly released output against a stale synchronized low sample on `sda_i` and falsely conclude that another device is holding SDA low. This raises `sda_interference` during an otherwise valid transaction.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs in host mode whenever the controller transitions SDA from driven low to released high and the synchronized SDA input still reflects the old low level for one or more cycles because of normal rise-time and synchronization delay. One observable case is a clean host read transaction on an uncontended bus: after the host releases SDA, the line is briefly sampled low, and the design incorrectly flags `sda_interference` instead of allowing the read transaction to complete.

problem_statement:
## Description
The OpenTitan Power Manager (`pwrmgr`) has a clock-domain crossing (CDC) bug in its escalation-reset handling path. The affected function is the logic that takes an escalation-reset request on `esc_rst_tx_i`, transfers it into the slow clock domain, and turns it into the escalation-triggered reset request path that drives the life-cycle reset request output (`rst_lc_req`).

## Expected Behavior
If `pwrmgr` observes an escalation-reset request on `esc_rst_tx_i`, it must capture that request even when the input is only a brief, non-permanent pulse that begins and ends between consecutive slow-clock sampling edges. After the request has been captured, the slow-domain escalation reset request must assert, `rst_lc_req` must assert, and the captured escalation request must remain asserted until reset clears it.

## Actual Behavior
When `esc_rst_tx_i` is only asserted briefly, `pwrmgr` can lose the request while synchronizing it into the slow clock domain. The escalation receiver can observe the pulse, but the slow-domain escalation reset request never asserts, `rst_lc_req` does not assert, and the escalation reset is effectively dropped.

## Affected Function
This affects `pwrmgr`'s escalation-reset CDC and request-latching logic between the escalation input and the slow-domain reset-request path.

## Trigger Condition
The bug is triggered when `esc_rst_tx_i` is a transient pulse asserted for fewer than two slow-clock cycles, so the pulse can occur entirely between slow-clock sampling edges instead of remaining continuously asserted.

title: fix(spi_device): Re-timing sck_cmdfifo_set clear time
body:
Related issue https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/11871

In previous design, the `sck_cmdfifo_set` signal is set by the ACK of
CMDFIFO write port and cleared by the FIFO DEPTH == 0.

THe clearing of FIFO depth depends on the SW processing time. This
commit revises it to CSb assertion pulse signal.

It is still bounded by the clock ratio between the SYS_CLK and the SCK.
SYS_CLK should not be 3 times slower than the SCK to correctly generate
the pulse signal within the opcode timeline.

repo.name: opentitan
repo.description: OpenTitan: Open source silicon root of trust

commits.message:
fix(spi_device): Missed Command Upload

This commit fixes one of the issue #11871

Problem:

    SW read incorrect opcode for Page Program.

Analysis
--------

The Page Program (0x02) opcode is adjacent to other commands that
SPI_DEVICE processes. So, the Datapath is fixed when the exact last beat
of the command opcode arrives. It is the second half of the 7th SCK.

The command parser activates Upload module at that time. However, the
top module switches the SRAM mux to the Upload module when the datapath
is latched by inverted SCK, which is right after the 8th posedge of SCK.

The Upload module, however, pushes the CMDFIFO entry (0x02 Page Program)
prior to 8th posedge of SCK to safely update the FIFO content as SCK
may not have 9th posedge if the SPI command is opcode only commands.
Examples are CHIP ERASE (0xC7), SECTOR ERASE, etc.

Resolution
----------

This commit revises the Mux design. Rather than using
`cmd_dp_sel_outclk`, it uses `cmd_dp_sel` (SCK clock) directly for the
SRAM mux. Other signals must be in inverted SCK clock domain to match
the output data phase.

Signed-off-by: Eunchan Kim <eunchan@opentitan.org>

fix(spi_device): Re-timing sck_cmdfifo_set clear time

Related issue #11871

In previous design, the `sck_cmdfifo_set` signal is set by the ACK of
CMDFIFO write port and cleared by the FIFO DEPTH == 0.

THe clearing of FIFO depth depends on the SW processing time. This
commit revises it to CSb assertion pulse signal.

It is still bounded by the clock ratio between the SYS_CLK and the SCK.
SYS_CLK should not be 3 times slower than the SCK to correctly generate
the pulse signal within the opcode timeline.

Signed-off-by: Eunchan Kim <eunchan@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] When and how should SW read cmdfifo, addrfifo, and payload buffer for correct data?
resolved_issues.body:
* spi_device should have a bit that indicates the completion of a SPI transaction and the FIFOs & the payload buffer are ready to be read from.
  * It looks like `cmdfifo_notempty` and `addrfifo_notempty` are updated independently during a SPI transaction.
  * According to the spec, `upload_payload_not_empty` in `INTR_STATE` register is updated after the transaction ends but it's not useful for commands without payloads.
  * `csb` in the `STATUS` register can possibly be used to check if a SPI transaction is complete but it is not clear whether sw can read from the FIFOs and the payload buffer right away.


* spi_device should ensure that values read from cmdfifo, addrfifo and payload are consistent with each other, e.g. they should always reflect the last transaction.
  * The address read from the address FIFO could belong to any command in the command FIFO (some commands don't have address fields), and similarly for the payload.
  * Please see [this thread](https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/11884#discussion_r842004669).

cc @cfrantz @a-will

python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

host_path = Path("hw/ip/spi_device/pre_dv/program/prog_passthrough_host.sv")
host_text = host_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
host_old = """  static task test_upload(output bit pass);
    SpiTransProgram trans;
    // Sequence
"""
host_new = """  static task test_upload(output bit pass);
    SpiTransProgram trans;
    pass = 1'b 1;

    // Sequence
"""
if host_old in host_text:
    host_text = host_text.replace(host_old, host_new, 1)
elif host_new not in host_text:
    raise SystemExit("host upload task patch point not found")
host_path.write_text(host_text, encoding="utf-8")

sw_path = Path("hw/ip/spi_device/pre_dv/program/prog_passthrough_sw.sv")
sw_text = sw_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
sw_new = """  static task test_upload();
    automatic logic [31:0] tl_rdata;
    automatic logic [ 7:0] opcode;

    wait(intr.upload_cmdfifo_not_empty);

    tlul_read(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_CMDFIFO_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );

    opcode = tl_rdata[7:0];
    $display("SW: Received Command: %2Xh", opcode);
    if (opcode != spi_device_pkg::CmdChipErase) begin
      $fatal(1, "SW: Unexpected Command: %2Xh / EXP(%2Xh)",
        opcode, spi_device_pkg::CmdChipErase);
    end

    tlul_write(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_INTR_STATE_OFFSET),
      1 << BitCmdfifoNotEmpty,
      4'b 1111
    );

    tlul_read(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_STATUS_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );
    if (tl_rdata[4:0] != 0) begin
      $display("SW: CMDFIFO not empty after fetching: %2d", tl_rdata[4:0]);
    end

    #3us;
    @(negedge clk);

    tlul_rmw(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_FLASH_STATUS_OFFSET),
      32'h 0,
      32'h 1
    );

    wait(intr.upload_cmdfifo_not_empty);

    tlul_read(
      clk, h2d, d2h,
      32'(spi_device_reg_pkg::SPI_DEVICE_UPLOAD_CMDFIFO_OFFSET),
      tl_rdata
    );

    opcode = tl_rdata[7:0];
    $display("SW: Received Command: %2Xh", opcode);
    if (opcode != spi_device_pkg::CmdPageProgram) begin
      $fatal(1, "SW: Unexpected Command: %2Xh / EXP(%2Xh)",
        opcode, spi_device_pkg::CmdPageProgram);
    end

  endtask : test_upload
"""
sw_pattern = re.compile(
    r"  static task test_upload\(\);\n.*?  endtask : test_upload\n",
    re.DOTALL,
)
if sw_pattern.search(sw_text):
    sw_text = sw_pattern.sub(sw_new, sw_text, count=1)
elif sw_new not in sw_text:
    raise SystemExit("sw upload task patch point not found")
sw_path.write_text(sw_text, encoding="utf-8")
PY

timeout 1800 bash -lc "

    --fixed-seed 1 \
    --build-seed 1 \
    --scratch-root '${SCRATCH_ROOT}' \
    >'${BUILD_LOG}' 2>&1

  cd '${SIM_DIR}'
  ./simv +ntb_random_seed=1 +TESTNAME=upload -l '${RUN_LOG}' >/dev/null 2>&1
"
flow_rc=$?
set -e

result="FAIL"

if [[ ${flow_rc} -eq 0 ]] && [[ -f "${RUN_LOG}" ]] && \
   grep -q "TEST PASSED CHECKS" "${RUN_LOG}" && ! grep -q "Fatal:" "${RUN_LOG}"; then
  result="PASS"
  exit_code=0
fi

if [[ -f "${BUILD_LOG}" ]]; then
  cat "${BUILD_LOG}"
fi

if [[ -f "${RUN_LOG}" ]]; then
  cat "${RUN_LOG}"
fi

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_START"

echo "HWE_BENCH_RESULTS_END"

problem_statement:
## Description
In the OpenTitan SPI Device IP's flash Passthrough mode, where selected SPI flash commands are forwarded to flash but also uploaded to software, the command upload path does not always preserve transaction boundaries. After software consumes one uploaded command, later bus activity can leave the upload notification associated with the old transaction instead of the next completed uploaded transaction.

## Expected Behavior
Each uploaded SPI flash transaction must be reported exactly once after chip-select (CSb) is deasserted for that transaction. Once software reads an opcode from `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` and clears the corresponding `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` interrupt, later non-uploaded transactions such as `READ_STATUS` must not re-assert that interrupt or expose a stale command entry. When the next uploaded transaction completes, software must receive a new `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` event, and reading `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` must return the opcode for that new transaction.

## Actual Behavior
If software first consumes an uploaded opcode-only command such as `CHIP_ERASE`, intervening hardware-handled `READ_STATUS` transactions can leave the upload indication tied to the earlier command. The next wait for `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty` may therefore wake on a stale event, and reading `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` can return `0x00` or the previous opcode instead of the opcode for the next uploaded command. In a later uploaded `PAGE_PROGRAM` transaction, software can therefore miss the new upload or read the stale erase opcode rather than `PAGE_PROGRAM`.

## Affected Function
The affected logic is the SPI Device IP flash command upload path in Passthrough mode, specifically the software-visible command reporting mechanism through `UPLOAD_CMDFIFO` and `upload_cmdfifo_not_empty`.

## Trigger Condition
This occurs when an uploaded command that ends after the opcode phase, such as `CHIP_ERASE`, is followed by one or more non-uploaded `READ_STATUS` polling transactions, and then another uploaded command such as `PAGE_PROGRAM`. The failure depends on software having already read the earlier uploaded command and cleared its interrupt before the later uploaded command arrives.

title: [flash_ctrl] Select appropriate ready's based on request source
body:
- fixes https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/issues/12381
- the previous design used the read stage's ready for arbitration.
  Due to the way the design is currently done, the read stage ready
  is actually dependent on the the downstream flash macro actually
  ack-ing the transaction.  To fix this, we would need to de-couple
  the req/ack interface on the side facing the phy and the side facing
  the macro.  While this is doable, it would also require us to latch
  incoming bus attributes.  However, there is not a lot to gain by doing
  so, because as long as the flash has not responded, the next read
  cannot proceed anyways.
- This dependency can cause program/erase operations to lock-up if the
  the downstream macro does not always keep ack asserted when idle (in
  effect behaving more like ready).
- Even though the above fix would be cleaner long term, the quick fix is
  simply to pick the appropriate ready for host and controller operations
  separately.

resolved_issues.title: Smoke test failing in the closed-source due to changes in the OS design
resolved_issues.body:
Hi,

Before everything, is it possible you'll add me as CC to the flash_ctrl's design PRs? It will help me to expect issues or things I need to update in the closed-source DV.

First of all, it seems the flash_ctrl prog_fifo depth has been changed in the flash_ctrl_env_pkg from 16 to 4, even though in the flash_ctrl spec is stated to still be 16. Is that intentional?
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/tb/tb.sv#L94-L98
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/dv/env/flash_ctrl_env_pkg.sv#L34-L35
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78012616/165791068-5483a74b-f86e-49e4-a17b-49e96751deea.png)


Secondly and more important, it seems that some changes that were done in the flash_ctrl files are causing some issues.
Before the full description, in order to reproduce the issue run flash_ctrl_smoke test in the closed-source env (and in the OS as well, to understand the difference). Notice that this issue happens in program transactions, so there is a some small chance the random smoke test will not create a program scenario, so it's better to run a few to make sure.

**Description:**
All program transactions are failing in the closed-source environment due to that program requests are initiated in the flash_ctrl but are blocked from being sent to the inner closed-source hierarchy.
It seems that in order to send prog_i to the inner hierarchies, the signal state_d in file flash_phy_core should be set to StCtrlProg:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv#L298-L306
For state_d to change from idle to prog:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_core.sv#L283-L284
Now, while prog_i is 1 as expected, ctrl_gnt stays 0.
This comes from:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree_dup.sv#L98-L99
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/prim/rtl/prim_arbiter_tree.sv#L124-L126
While the 2 first signals are 1 as needed, the ready signal isn't and comes from:
https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/blob/48e4bb6fca893b2065ac14299369b2aa4739f48e/hw/ip/flash_ctrl/rtl/flash_phy_rd.sv#L333-L335
All of those signals are as needed, except the ack. Notice that in order for the ready to be 1 the ack signal coming from the inner hierarchy should be 1, which isn't seems reasonable. Since no request was sent to the inner hierarchy by now, why would it send an acknowledge?
What comes from this is a loop - the request waits for an acknowledge which waits for a request.

In addition, it seems that the smoke test is passing in the OS env. The reason it's passing is because for some reason the acknowledge seems to always come before the request:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78012616/165788041-8ba36cc3-b7f0-4f12-b579-9b03dae0cc73.png)

Thanks!

@@ -20,6 +20,9 @@ module prim_arbiter_tree_dup #(

   parameter bit EnDataPort = 1,
 
+  // if arbiter has fixed priority

   // Derived parameters
   localparam int IdxW = $clog2(N)
 ) (
@@ -77,22 +80,43 @@ module prim_arbiter_tree_dup #(
       );
     end
 
-    prim_arbiter_tree #(
-      .N(N),
-      .DW(DW),
-      .EnDataPort(EnDataPort)
-    ) u_arb (

#!/bin/bash
set -e

# Stage 1: checkout base_sha in a clean workspace (+submodules)
cd /home/opentitan
git reset --hard
git clean -fdx
git checkout b2fed682d4b0617078c16527c69f72fca7f895f8
git submodule update --init --recursive

PREP_DIR=/home/opentitan/.prepare
rm -rf "$PREP_DIR"
mkdir -p "$PREP_DIR"

# Stage 2: install repository apt dependencies (if present)
export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
if [[ -f apt-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing apt dependencies from apt-requirements.txt"
  cp apt-requirements.txt "$PREP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
  sed -i -e '/^$/d' -e '/^#/d' -e 's/#.*//' "$PREP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
  if [[ -s "$PREP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt" ]]; then
    apt-get update
    xargs -r apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends < "$PREP_DIR/apt-requirements.txt"
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
  else
    echo "[INFO] apt-requirements.txt is empty after filtering comments"
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] apt-requirements.txt not found at base_sha; skipping repo-specific apt install"
fi

# Stage 3: install project-specific Python dependencies from the checked-out repo
if [[ -f python-requirements.txt ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Python deps from python-requirements.txt"
  python -m pip install -U pip "setuptools<66.0.0"
  cp python-requirements.txt "$PREP_DIR/python-requirements.txt"
  python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re

path = Path("/home/opentitan/.prepare/python-requirements.txt")
lines = []
for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines():
    stripped = line.strip()
    if stripped in {
        "types-dataclasses",
        "types-pkg_resources",
    }:
        continue
    line = re.sub(r'(#egg=[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)\s+[<>=!~].*', r'\1', line)
    lines.append(line)
path.write_text("\n".join(lines) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
PY
  python -m pip install -r "$PREP_DIR/python-requirements.txt" --no-warn-script-location
else
  echo "[ERROR] python-requirements.txt not found at base_sha"
  exit 1
fi

# Stage 4: install RISC-V toolchain + Verible, then persist their PATH
if [[ -f util/get-toolchain.py ]]; then
  toolchain_version=""
  if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
    toolchain_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
  fi

  echo "[INFO] Installing RISC-V toolchain via util/get-toolchain.py"
  if [[ -n "$toolchain_version" ]]; then
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update -r "$toolchain_version"
  else
    echo "[WARN] RISCV_TOOLCHAIN_TAR_VERSION not found; falling back to util/get-toolchain.py defaults"
    python util/get-toolchain.py --update
  fi
else
  echo "[WARN] util/get-toolchain.py not found at base_sha; skipping RISC-V toolchain install"
fi

verible_version=""
if [[ -f util/container/Dockerfile ]]; then
  verible_version="$(sed -n 's/^ARG VERIBLE_VERSION=//p' util/container/Dockerfile | head -n1)"
fi

if [[ -n "$verible_version" ]]; then
  echo "[INFO] Installing Verible ${verible_version}"
  rm -rf /tools/verible
  mkdir -p /tools/verible
  curl -f -Ls -o "$PREP_DIR/verible.tar.gz" \
    "https://github.com/chipsalliance/verible/releases/download/${verible_version}/verible-${verible_version}-Ubuntu-18.04-bionic-x86_64.tar.gz"
  tar -C /tools/verible -xf "$PREP_DIR/verible.tar.gz" --strip-components=1
else
  echo "[WARN] Unable to determine Verible version from util/container/Dockerfile"
fi

cat > /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh <<'EOF'
for d in /tools/riscv/bin /tools/verible/bin; do
  [ -d "$d" ] && export PATH="$d:$PATH"
done
EOF

if ! grep -q "/etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" /etc/opentitan_bash_env; then
  echo "source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh" >> /etc/opentitan_bash_env
fi
source /etc/opentitan_tools_path.sh

python -m pip show edalize fusesoc hjson >/dev/null
if command -v riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] RISC-V toolchain ready: $(riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc not found after Stage 4"
fi
if command -v verible-verilog-lint >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[INFO] Verible ready: $(verible-verilog-lint --version | head -n1)"
else
  echo "[WARN] verible-verilog-lint not found after Stage 4"
fi
problem_statement:
## Description
The bug is in OpenTitan's flash controller (`flash_ctrl`), specifically in `flash_phy_core`, the block that arbitrates between an external host-side flash access and an internal controller-initiated flash operation before forwarding a request to the downstream flash macro.

## Expected Behavior
When the controller side issues an erase request while the `flash_phy_core` read stage is idle and there is no competing host-side request, `flash_phy_core` must grant that controller request and forward the corresponding erase request to the flash macro. The flash macro's acknowledge (`ack`) signal may legally remain low while idle and only assert after a request is presented, so controller-side progress must not depend on `ack` already being asserted before the request is sent.

## Actual Behavior
A controller-originated erase request can deadlock inside `flash_phy_core`. The controller request waits for a grant/readiness condition that is itself derived from the downstream flash macro's `ack`, while the flash macro waits to see the erase request before asserting `ack`. As a result, the erase request never reaches the flash macro and the controller operation never completes.

## Affected Function
The affected functionality is the `flash_ctrl` `flash_phy_core` arbitration and request handoff for controller-side erase operations to the downstream flash macro.

## Trigger Conditions
The failure occurs when a controller-side erase operation, including page erase, is issued while the `flash_phy_core` read stage is idle, no host-side request is competing for arbitration, and the downstream flash macro uses a request/acknowledge handshake where `ack` is asserted only after a request is presented rather than being held high while idle.

resolved_issues.body:
Currently the interrupt clock domain crossing uses a primitive with the unfortunate property that multiple triggers on the always on clock side while the gated clock is off can cause difficult to predict results.
The first trigger sets the interrupt, a second occurring during a gated period clears the interrupt again, a third sets it again and so on.
This leads to unexpected results.

Perhaps a scheme where all the interrupt logic is performed on the always on side, then copied via a request/acknowledge type CDC to the gated side, would be preferable.

I've re-enabled interrupts for test adc_ctrl_clock_gating in this PR https://github.com/lowRISC/opentitan/pull/11760

problem_statement:
## Description
The ADC Controller has an interrupt clock-domain crossing bug in the path that carries filter-match events from the always-on clock domain into the gated main clock domain.

## Expected Behavior
If an enabled filter-match event occurs while the main ADC interrupt/register clock is gated off, that event must remain pending until the main clock resumes. Repeated pulses from the same filter-match source during the gated interval must not cancel or clear the pending interrupt. Once the main clock is running again, the corresponding ADC interrupt-status bit and the top-level interrupt pending state must both be asserted.

## Actual Behavior
When the same filter-match source pulses multiple times while the main clock is gated, the current synchronization logic can toggle the pending state on each pulse. After an even number of pulses during one gated interval, the ADC Controller can resume with no pending interrupt, even though an enabled filter-match event occurred.

## Affected Function
ADC Controller interrupt handling for filter-match events that are generated in the always-on clock domain but must update interrupt status and interrupt pending state in the gated main clock domain.

## Trigger Condition
This is triggered when the ADC Controller enters a state where the main clock domain is gated but the always-on ADC logic continues running, and the same enabled filter-match interrupt source fires multiple times before the main clock domain is ungated.

title: [spi_device] Change `addr_latched` to a pulse signal
body:
Problem:

    `addr_latched_i` in `spid_readsram` module is expected to be a pulse
    signal. The `spi_readcmd` module generates the signal as a level by
    comparing `addr_cnt_d` with all zero value.

    As a result, the `strb` register in `spid_readsram` follows the
    current address, which is increased by when a byte is sent to the
    host system. However, the `spid_readsram` logic pushes the data into
    the FIFO already. As the FIFO depth is 2, one more entry has been
    added to the FIFO, which results the host system sees the a byte has
    been shifted.

Resolution:

    Revised the `addr_latched` logic to be a pulse. Either `addr_cnt_d`
    or `addr_latched` can be revised. I chose the latter. Latching the
    latched signal and generated a pulse.

This PR contains #11829  Please review the last commit only. I will rebase once the PR is merged

commits.message:
[spi_device] Change addr_latched as a pulse

Problem:

    `addr_latched_i` in `spid_readsram` module is expected to be a pulse
    signal. The `spi_readcmd` module generates the signal as a level by
    comparing `addr_cnt_d` with all zero value.

    As a result, the `strb` register in `spid_readsram` follows the
    current address, which is increased by when a byte is sent to the
    host system. However, the `spid_readsram` logic pushes the data into
    the FIFO already. As the FIFO depth is 2, one more entry has been
    added to the FIFO, which results the host system sees the a byte has
    been shifted.

Resolution:

    Revised the `addr_latched` logic to be a pulse. Either `addr_cnt_d`
    or `addr_latched` can be revised. I chose the latter. Latching the
    latched signal and generated a pulse.

Signed-off-by: Eunchan Kim <eunchan@opentitan.org>

resolved_issues.title: [spi_device] Direct Testcase for SFDP
resolved_issues.body:
This PR implements the testcase for SPI_DEVICE SFDP command.

The return data is not correct. I will analyze the waveform and design then fix in following PRs.

fix_patch:
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_readcmd.sv b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_readcmd.sv
index a6d89096a5453..e32d2d8512420 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_readcmd.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spi_readcmd.sv
@@ -392,7 +392,23 @@ module spi_readcmd
   assign addr_ready_in_word     = (addr_cnt_d == 5'd 2);
   assign addr_ready_in_halfword = (addr_cnt_d == 5'd 1);
 
-  assign addr_latched = (addr_cnt_d == 5'd 0);
+  // addr_latched should be a pulse to be used in spid_readsram
+  logic  addr_latched_d;
+  assign addr_latched_d = (addr_cnt_d == 5'd 0);
+
+  prim_edge_detector #(
+    .Width      (1),
+    .ResetValue (1'b 0),
+    .EnSync     (1'b 0)
+  ) u_addr_latch_pulse (
+    .clk_i,
+    .rst_ni,
+
+    .d_i               (addr_latched_d),
+    .q_sync_o          (              ),
+    .q_posedge_pulse_o (addr_latched  ),
+    .q_negedge_pulse_o (              )
+  );
 
   assign cmdinfo_addr_mode = get_addr_mode(cmd_info_i, addr_4b_en_i);
 
diff --git a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spid_readsram.sv b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spid_readsram.sv
index cec7d50501a52..b9f0dea002aa0 100644
--- a/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spid_readsram.sv
+++ b/hw/ip/spi_device/rtl/spid_readsram.sv
@@ -351,4 +351,7 @@ module spid_readsram
   // strb_set is asserted together with sram_req or follows the req
   `ASSUME(ReqStrbRelation_M, sram_read_req_i |-> ##[0:2] addr_latched_i)
 
+  // Address latched signal is a pulse signal
+  `ASSUME(AddrLatchedPulse_M, addr_latched_i |=> !addr_latched_i)
+
 endmodule : spid_readsram
